personality: Ancient, hungry and fair in her own terrible way. She keeps her word, and she eats those who waste her time.
voice: Ask too much and you grow old here.

cards.title: The Old Woman of the Forest
cards.text: Deep in the forest stands her house, fenced with human bones, with a skull on every stake. At night the skulls' eyes burn and light the clearing like noon. Three riders serve her: a white one who brings the bright day, a red one who is the sun, and a black one who is the dark night. She is older than any of them, and she eats those who displease her.

source.author: collected by A. N. Afanasyev, 1855–67; English by Leonard A. Magnus, 1915

cards.title: The Girl Who Came for Fire
cards.text: One night a merchant's daughter, Vasilisa, came to her gate. Her cruel stepmother had sent her to fetch fire from Baba Yaga, hoping she would never return. The witch came home riding her mortar, steering with her pestle. She agreed to give the girl fire if she worked for it, and set her impossible tasks. If one was left undone, she would eat her.

source.author: collected by A. N. Afanasyev, 1855–67; English by Leonard A. Magnus, 1915

cards.title: The Blessing
cards.text: Every task was done. The witch asked how, and Vasilisa said her dead mother's blessing helped her. Baba Yaga would not keep a blessed girl in her house, so she sent her home with what she had come for: a skull with burning eyes. That night its stare burned the stepmother and her daughters to ashes. Baba Yaga stayed in her forest, and is there still.

source.author: collected by A. N. Afanasyev, 1855–67; English by Leonard A. Magnus, 1915
